message.content:
A common example of a **multinucleated** cell is a *skeletal muscle fiber* (also called a myocyte).  
These elongated cells fuse together during development so each resulting fiber contains many nuclei—one at each end of its long cytoplasmic domain—to support high metabolic demand and protein synthesis across the entire length of the fiber.  

Other notable multinucleated cells include:

| Cell Type | Typical Function |
|-----------|------------------|
| Osteoclast | Bone resorption – breaks down bone matrix |
| Syncytiotrophoblast | Forms part of the placenta’s outer layer, facilitating nutrient exchange between mother and fetus |
| Myofibers (muscle) | Contractile tissue responsible for voluntary movement |

So if you’re looking for a “name” of such a cell, *skeletal muscle fiber* is one of the most well‑known examples.
